questions.q: In the real folder layout (prompts/, context/, evals/, CHANGELOG.md), what does the lesson say makes this a 'library' rather than just a folder of files?
options: Having exactly four folders
Using Markdown instead of plain text files
Storing everything in a single file instead of multiple folders
The CHANGELOG.md, which connects each prompt version to its actual eval results over time
questions.explain: The lesson states explicitly that the changelog is what turns a folder of files into an actual library — a dated record connecting each version to its real score.

questions.q: What belongs in the context/ folder according to this lesson?
options: The eval set and its test results
budget.md (the token budget worksheet) and any real tool schemas
The system prompt and task templates
Only the changelog
questions.explain: context/ holds budget.md (Lesson 13's worksheet shape) and tools.json with real tool schemas (Lesson 16), distinct from prompts/ and evals/.

questions.q: What is step 1 in the recommended build order for this capstone lesson?
options: Running automated tests before writing any prompts
Setting the regression baseline before anything else exists
Writing system.md and the task templates first, since there's nothing to budget or test without working prompts
Writing CHANGELOG.md before any prompt files exist
questions.explain: The build order starts with the prompts themselves (system.md + templates), since budgeting, testing, and logging all depend on having real prompts to work with first.

questions.q: According to the lesson, what should results/ (inside evals/) actually contain?
options: The actual output of running the automated testing loop, one file per test run
A written description of what testing would probably show
A copy of the eval_set.json file with no changes
Marketing copy about the prompt library
questions.explain: The lesson specifies results/ holds the real output of Lesson 19's automated testing loop for each run — actual results, not a description of expected results.

questions.q: Why does the lesson say having at least two versions logged in CHANGELOG.md matters by the end of this lesson?
options: Because a changelog requires a minimum of two entries by convention only
Because the course requires exactly two prompt versions and no more
Because two entries are needed to calculate a pass rate at all
Because it provides a real before-and-after needed for the A/B comparison and regression baseline covered in the next lesson
questions.explain: The lesson explains that two logged versions give you a real before and after, which is exactly what's needed for Lesson 24's wrap-up, building on the A/B and regression work from Chapter 4.
